multiplechoiceresponse.p: Which statement about an AI change is honest and usable?

choice.div: "The drafting part of your week shrinks; checking and client conversations grow; here is the training for both."
"Everyone will need to become an AI expert."

div.p: Task-level change is specific and defensible. Blanket reassurance is a promise a manager cannot keep.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: What is the right sequence before setting a productivity target?

choice.div: Rule, approved tool, training, then target.
Target first, then figure out the tooling.
Target and training at the same time.

div.p: People under a target with no approved route will choose the fastest unsafe option.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: An experienced employee says the tool will not work for their cases. What should the manager do first?

choice.div: Ask which case would break it and test that case.
Move the employee to another team.

div.p: Resistance often names a real exception. Testing it is free quality assurance.

choiceresponse.p: Which support does a team need during an AI change? Select all that apply.

choice.div: A one-page rule on what may be assisted.
A blame-free route to report failures.
A pledge that no role will ever change.

div.p: Rules, skill, a workable route and psychological safety are the supports. A pledge about roles cannot be kept.
